source_text: Klagel. Jerem. 1, 11. Ἐστέναζον διὰ λιμὸν καὶ μικρᾶς ἕνεκα βρώσεως ψυχὴν ἐπιστρεφούσης ἐκλείπουσαν παρεῖχον τὰ τιμιώτατα. πῶς δὲ τὰ προρρηθέντα ἐπιθυμήματα παρὰ τῶν πολεμίων ἀπενεχθέντα παρεῖχον εἰς ὠνὴν τροφῆς; ἀλλ᾿ >ἐξέτεινε μὲν ὁ ἐχθρὸς ἐπὶ πάντα τὴν χεῖρα<, κορεσθεὶς δὲ τῷ λαβεῖν ἅπερ ἤθελε, τὰ λοιπὰ καταλέλοιπεν. ἀνθ’ ὧν ἐπρίαντο τὴν τροφήν.
pass_a_gloss: They were groaning because of famine, and for the sake of a small bit of food that turns back a failing soul they were giving over the most honorable things. And how were they giving the aforementioned epithymēmata / desirable things—carried off by the enemies—unto purchase of food? But “the enemy stretched out the hand upon all,” and having been filled by taking what he wanted, he left the rest; in exchange for which they bought the food.
pass_b_english: They were groaning because of famine, and for the sake of a small bit of food that turns back a failing soul they were giving over the most honorable things. And how were they giving the aforementioned desirable things—carried off by the enemies—unto purchase of food? But “the enemy stretched out the hand upon all,” (Lamentations 1:11) and having been filled by taking what he wanted, he left the rest; in exchange for which they bought the food.

choices.why: Origen’s image of the fallen soul as storm-tossed in Lam 1:8 commentary.

anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of Origen’s Greek Lamentations fragments. Sense checked against Klostermann GCS III. Modern English not copied. OET = no previous English translation.
